honest_c3: C1 HEXA_PY env override is INVISIBLE to general users — magnetic to friction. Documentation MUST surface this in bin/anima help, anima dialogue --help, and any onboarding docs. Without HEXA_PY explicit, the .venv-eeg auto-detect fallback (2) handles it for typical anima developers but breaks if developer has a different venv layout.

C2 The 2 spec-mandated fixes are NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for wrapper real-mode. A third architectural fix is required: either (a) augment the helper-emit code in mount.hexa::_write_helper with SentencePiece tokenizer fallback when AutoTokenizer fails, OR (b) route mount.hexa to invoke tool/transient_py/anima_dialogue_load.py directly instead of emitting its own helper. Both options are additive but exceed the 2-fix scope of this BG.

C3 BG-A's verdict (state/anima_dialogue_real_load_2026_05_05/verdict.json) underestimated the wrapper-blocker — claimed 'set HEXA_PY env + pass --model would unblock'. Empirical test refutes this: the third AutoTokenizer blocker is real and persistent regardless of HEXA_PY/model fixes.

C4 .venv-eeg auto-detect (fallback 2 of new resolver chain) creates implicit coupling — if user renames or removes .venv-eeg, the resolver silently falls through to homebrew python3, which has the OMP libomp double-init that breaks AutoModelForCausalLM. C5 Direct invoke of anima_dialogue_load.py via BG-A path REMAINS the canonical real-mode entry until the wrapper is unblocked. Document this as the sanctioned probe interface in any --help output or the spec doc. The wrapper at bin/anima-core-dialogue.bash is currently best-effort fallback infrastructure, not a real-mode entry point.
